name: ai_api_cost
title: AI API cost
description: Estimate API workload costs in USD per request, day and month, with rates and dated snapshot provenance. Use for token budgets; use ai_subscription_stack_cost for chat or coding subscriptions. Model IDs use providerId/id from https://operatornest.com/api/models?subset=pricing, filtered to the MCP catalog; the OSS bundle lists accepted IDs in src/data/pricing-snapshot.json. Rates stay offline until the catalog is updated; missing rates return null. Cached tokens are part of total input; published batch and long-context rates apply only when eligible. Non-token charges are excluded.

inputTokens.description: Total input tokens per request, including cached input tokens.

cachedInputTokens.description: Cached portion of inputTokens per request; must not exceed inputTokens. Use 0 without caching.

requestsPerDay.description: Requests used to scale the daily estimate, independent of requestsPerMonth.

requestsPerMonth.description: Requests used to scale the monthly estimate; not inferred from the daily count.

modelIds.description: Unique providerId/id values from the MCP pricing catalog. Unknown or unavailable IDs fail validation.

items.description: Model ID accepted by the MCP pricing catalog.
Selected model ID with a published batch discount.

batchModelIds.description: Optional subset of modelIds to price with published batch discounts. Omission or [] uses standard rates; IDs without a published discount are rejected.

name: meeting_time_zones
title: Meeting time zones
description: Find shared 30-minute meeting slots inside 09:00–17:00 for 2–8 participants. Use to compare workday overlap; use recurring_schedule for repeating task calendars or cron_next_runs for scheduler previews. Returns all candidates, overlap count and up to three best slots ranked nearest to each person’s 13:00, with UTC starts and local labels. The date belongs to the first participant’s zone; daylight saving uses runtime IANA data. No calendar availability or holiday lookup, invitations or calendar writes.

date.description: Meeting date in the first person’s local time zone, from 2000-01-01 to 2100-12-31.

people.description: Participants in display order. The first person determines the local date; all must fit a full half-hour inside 09:00–17:00.

name.description: Participant label used in the returned local-time display.

zone.description: IANA time zone supported by Intl.DateTimeFormat.

name: recurring_schedule
title: Recurring schedule
description: Prepare weekly, biweekly or monthly task calendars and estimate monthly effort for up to 20 tasks. Use to draft a recurring work plan; use cron_next_runs to preview existing cron syntax or meeting_time_zones for shared workday slots. Returns monthly hours, first dates, recurrence rules and an RFC 5545 calendar. Times float in the importing calendar’s local zone; weekly estimates use 52/12 runs per month and biweekly 26/12. owner is a planning label, with no assignment or execution. No calendar is updated; an empty task list returns zero hours and no events.

startDate.description: Earliest date for the first occurrence of each task, from 2000-01-01 to 2100-12-31.

tasks.description: Tasks to include in the estimate and calendar. [] returns zero hours and a calendar with no events.

title.description: Task label used as the calendar event summary.

frequency.description: Repeat every week, every two weeks from the first matching weekday, or every month.

day.description: Weekday for weekly/biweekly tasks. Required but ignored for monthly tasks.

monthday.description: Day of month for monthly tasks, limited to dates present in every month. Required but ignored for weekly/biweekly tasks.

minutes.description: Estimated minutes per run; used for event duration and monthly hours.

time.description: 24-hour HH:mm start time, floating in the importing calendar’s local time zone.

owner.description: Planning label: delegate to an operator, keep for yourself, or decide later. Included in the calendar note; does not assign or execute work.

name: ai_subscription_stack_cost
title: AI subscription stack cost
description: Total selected AI chat and coding subscriptions in USD and identify overlapping capabilities. Use to review a subscription stack; use ai_api_cost for API token charges. Select unique planIds from the schema enum; [] returns zero totals and no plans. Returns monthly and annual totals, selected plans, capability groups and dated official sources. Annual totals use published annual billing or twelve monthly charges; taxes, regional differences and promotions are excluded. Bundled rates are dated estimates, without live billing lookup or subscription changes.

name: cron_next_runs
title: Cron next runs
description: Preview up to 10 cron matches strictly after a supplied UTC instant, within a 366-day search. Use to check existing scheduler syntax; use recurring_schedule to draft task recurrence calendars or meeting_time_zones for participant overlap. Returns UTC starts, local labels, normalized inputs and a dated syntax source; fewer matches or [] means the search window ended. Supports numeric stars, lists, ranges, steps and weekday names in the selected dialect; rejects L, W, # and named months. cloudflare requires UTC; other zones follow runtime daylight saving transitions. No schedule is installed or run.

expression.description: Cron fields in the selected dialect: five for github/cloudflare, six or seven for quartz, six for aws (optional cron(...) wrapper). Supports *, lists, ranges, steps and weekday names; rejects L, W, # and named months. Quartz/aws require ? in exactly one day field.

dialect.description: Scheduler syntax and weekday numbering. github uses 0 or 7 for Sunday and 1–6 for Monday–Saturday; the others use 1–7 for Sunday–Saturday.

zone.description: IANA time zone for matching local cron fields. cloudflare requires UTC. Daylight saving transitions follow the runtime time-zone database.

after.description: UTC ISO instant from 2000 through 2100; matches are strictly after this instant. Only Z offsets are accepted.

count.description: Maximum matches to return. The list may be shorter or empty if no further matches occur within the 366-day search.
